items.title: Northwest Notes: Peterson, Thunder Injuries, McDaniels, Ball
items.summary: After a brutal start, the Jazz are starting to be more competitive, a trend that corresponds with the improved play from rookie Darryn Peterson. On Friday, Utah lost to the Suns after cutting the game to four in the last minute, ending a two-game winning streak. While the team dug itself a hole, a bright spot was rookie Darryn Peterson recording his first career double-double, with 20 points, 10 rebounds, eight assists, and two steals. He struggled from the field, shooting just 7-of-20, but still found ways to be a positive contributor all over the floor, Na’Andre Emerson writes for Deseret News. After the game, Suns star Devin Booker gave him his jersey, calling him “my fav rook,” Shreyas Laddha writes for the Salt Lake Tribune. Booker is a player that Peterson has credited as being a model for his own game. “That’s what it is all about, inspiring that next generation,” Booker said…

items.title: Five Two-Way Players Making Early Cases For Promotions
items.summary: Two-way contracts allow NBA teams to carry three extra players in addition to the 15 on their regular season roster. These players generally bounce back and forth between the NBA and G League, but remain under team control and can’t be poached by rival franchises. You can check out our glossary entry to learn more about two-way contracts, but here are some key points to remember: Two-way players are eligible to be active for up to 50 of their team’s 82 regular season games. If a team isn’t carrying a full 15-man standard roster, its two-way players can only be active for a combined 90 “under-15” games. Players on two-way contracts will earn $678,882 in 2026/27, half of the rookie minimum. Two-way contracts can’t be signed after March 4. Two-way players are ineligible to play in the postseason (including play-in games) unless they’re promoted to the standard 15-man roster, which can…

The update on Powell is pretty vague, and hamstring are notoriously tricky, but it’s noteworthy that the team used “mild” to describe the strain, tweets K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network. Johnson expects the Bulls to give a more definitive return timeline for Powell after he’s reexamined.
